findings.claim: kmctl_search_files numbers lines with str.splitlines(), which also breaks on \r, \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85 and U+2028, while kmctl_read_file numbers lines by \n. In a file holding a form feed or a lone \r, search reports a different line number than read for the same line, and the auditor cites path:line from search as evidence.

The whole prompt (skills, auditor text and the due list) goes to hermes as one argv string after -z. Linux caps one argument at 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), so a due list of roughly 800 or more concepts makes exec fail with E2BIG; the run then fails with "hermes exited 126" instead of a message that says why. The old script sent the prompt on stdin, so this ceiling is new.

The script unsets HERMES_PROFILE, HERMES_CONFIG, HERMES_ENV and HERMES_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS, but Hermes 0.19.0 also reads HERMES_MANAGED_DIR (hermes_cli/managed_scope.py), a managed config and .env applied last with override, which beats the config the script writes. It belongs in the same unset list.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.
The plugin holds against every path escape I tried, the script keeps every guard, the docs agree with the code, and the gates are green on my own run.

Three findings remain, none blocking: search and read can number the same line differently (f1), the prompt in argv has a size ceiling the old stdin path did not have (f2), and one more Hermes config variable belongs in the unset list (f3).
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format and tests pass, and r1 to r7 pass.
Result: `stamp green: ce97ede2cbe85dcf1072f462ccfc1dc5238633ba71a9de378909a6fd92e65d69`.
Plugin probes (a recording ctx on action/hermes/kmctl-read/__init__.py, outside the repo).

Each of these is refused with "outside the repository": `..`, an absolute path outside, a file symlink out, a folder symlink out, a symlink to /proc/self and then `environ`, /proc/self/environ, ~/.bashrc, `/` and `..` for listing.
A NUL byte and a lone surrogate in a path come back as errors, not exceptions.
A FIFO and a folder are "not a file".
No KMCTL_READ_ROOT, an empty one or a relative one refuses everything.
A binary file reads as replacement text within the cap.
A 5 MB one-line file returns about 100 KB with a cut note.
A search over 700 matching files stops at 200 matches, and a listing stops at 500 files, each with a note.
`--pre=rm` and `(a+)+$` are matched as plain text in 0.02 s.
The walk does not follow a symlinked folder and skips a file symlink that points out.
Every result is a str.
TOCTOU between the check and open needs a writer, and the model has none, so it is not reachable.
Eval rows: I read each test the rows run.
r1 checks the flags, the config's base_url, the `${VAR}` key, that the literal key is absent, that HOME is not the runner's, and that no vendor is named.

r2 checks `-t kmctl_read` once, that the installed plugin equals the source, plugins.enabled, an empty safe root outside the repo, timeout in the code, and that a sleeping stub is stopped by a 2 s limit, plus the workflow's timeout-minutes and the mode help.
r3's tests cover every clause of its fails_when, including the HOME config, /proc/PID/environ, regex timing and the import ban.
r4 checks every text, the absolute path and that the footer is cut.
r5 has no `uses: ./`, has both installs and both scripts, and has the four inputs with no anthropic_api_key.
r7 checks Hermes, provider, the 0005 link, Claude Code and okf_validate.
r8 (judgment): I re-ran spike 3's script against the current worktree with the real Hermes 0.19.0 in the scratch install.
Both requests that carried tools offered exactly the three kmctl tools.
write_file, patch, terminal and execute_code got "does not exist".
The fixture stayed unchanged with git status clean.
The /proc/self/environ read and search were refused without the key, and the finding reached the summary and the issue body.
RESULT: holds.
The row holds.

Script: the event guard, the token and extraheader guards, the model, URL and key-name checks, the unshallow fetch, the scope filter, the fresh HOME under mktemp (outside the repository root), and the config holding `${KEY_ENV}` and never the key are all there.
The unset list, timeout with --kill-after, and the 124/137 message are there too.
I checked that Hermes' own .env loading uses its install folder and HERMES_HOME, not the audited repository's working folder.

action.yml and the workflow run the same commands: `uv tool install` kmctl, `uv tool install --python 3.12 hermes-agent==0.19.0`, the audit script with the four settings, and the issue step, which alone holds GH_TOKEN.

Docs: ADR 0010 (context, decision, rejected options, consequences), ADR 0005's dated Correction, the overview diagram, prose and Depicts, both indexes, the log, and the how-to's table, example, timeout text and Ollama num_ctx note.
They agree with the code.
Nothing in the repo still tells users to set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

f1 (bug, not blocking): demonstrated with `printf 'a\x0cb
cd
target
'`.
Search returns `x.txt:5: target` and read returns `3|target`.
The fix is to split the decoded text on "\n" only (and strip a trailing "\r"), matching read_file.
Separately, read_file counts a line longer than 100 KB as two numbered chunks, which shifts later numbers too.
Its docstring says the line is split, but not that the numbering shifts.
f2 (hardening, not blocking): `-z` in Hermes 0.19.0 takes no stdin or file form that I could find.
A length check before the call, with a clear message, would turn the E2BIG into an error that says why.
This is far off for real bundles: this repo's due list is 1.7 KB for 12 concepts.
f3 (hardening, not blocking): add HERMES_MANAGED_DIR to the `unset` line.
/etc/hermes is also read when present; that is the runner's own setup, and a note in the comment would cover it.
Dropping ripgrep differs from the plan's text ("The runner installs ripgrep"), but it is right.
No kmctl tool runs a program, and nothing else in the run calls rg.
The narrow N999 per-file ignore is justified: Hermes names a plugin by its hyphenated folder, and nothing imports it.
Placeholder settings: I would keep `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` with `qwen/qwen3-coder`.
OpenRouter is itself a router to many vendors, so it is no tie to one, and a working value shows the shape better than `https://YOUR-ENDPOINT/v1`.
One risk: someone who sets AUDIT_API_KEY to another vendor's key before changing base_url sends that key to OpenRouter.
A one-line warning in the workflow comment ("the key is sent to base_url") would cover it.
READ_BYTES of 100 KB is about 25K tokens, a large share of the 64K context the how-to recommends for Ollama.
Worth watching on small models; no change asked.
`ignore_case` takes any truthy value, so the string "false" turns folding on.
Models send JSON booleans, so this is harmless.
